decisions.executionNote: Begin smooth elbow-up reorientation above each side; approach left blue and right red pieces without crossing arms.
Finish top-down orientation and center above the left blue and right red, maintaining separate workspaces.
Use wrist views to refine centering while lowering; yaw the left gripper to the blue bar's long axis. Keep both open pending alignment check.
Fine-center both pieces between the fingers, close fully, and make a short vertical test lift to assess retention from RGB.
Both pieces appear retained. Lift clear, then carry the red ring above the third peg; keep the left arm clear while holding its blue bar.
Refine ring-to-third-peg alignment using the visible peg and descend slowly; retain both grasps pending insertion evidence.
The third peg is visible through the ring opening. Lower the remaining short seating distance, then release and inspect before withdrawing.
Ring tilted after release, so insertion is unconfirmed. Withdraw the right gripper to inspect; bring the held blue bar closer while keeping arms separated.
Bring the blue bar above the second peg and pause high enough to refine alignment from its hole and the peg; leave the right arm out of the way.
The second peg is visible at the blue bar's hole. Lower vertically in small increments while retaining the grasp, then check seating before release.
Blue is visibly threaded onto its peg. Release and withdraw the left arm toward the next blue; approach the tilted red ring from above with the right arm for correction.
Approach the next left blue bar and the tilted red ring with open fingers. The red is not seated; reposition for a recovery grasp rather than assuming completion.
Refine the second blue grasp and close both grippers. Make short test lifts, especially for the tilted red, before further transport.
Blue was held off-center, so set down briefly and regrasp nearer its hole. Lift the edge-held red clear into the right workspace for flattening and a fresh top-down grasp.
The blue remained on the table; reopen and descend for a centered fresh grasp. Gradually rotate the retained edge-held red toward horizontal in clear right-side space.
Center and regrasp the blue at tabletop height, then test lift. Continue gently flattening the retained red ring and lowering it over clear table for a reset.
Second blue is now retained. Carry it above the second peg. Release the flattened red over clear table, then retract and restore the right gripper toward top-down.
Fine-align the second blue over its peg and lower toward the first bar. Restore the right gripper to top-down while approaching the reset red ring.
The second blue may be caught on the peg rim. Lift slightly, correct the fore-aft offset, and reseat without opening. Lower the right gripper toward the red for a fresh centered grasp.
The blue hole now surrounds the peg; open and withdraw to check whether it settles flat. Finish centering the red at tabletop height, close, and test-lift.
Red is retained flat after the reset. Carry it high over the third peg, accounting for its grasp offset. Move the left arm clear toward the remaining left ring.
Use the visible third-peg tip to correct the red ring's lateral alignment and descend cautiously. Approach the remaining left ring with open fingers.
The red hole is centered over the third peg. Lower slowly toward the base without releasing. Center and test-grasp the remaining ring with the left arm.
The red is catching the peg rather than seating, and a blue bar has fallen. Lift the red clear, correct rightward and backward alignment, and retry above the peg without forcing downward.
Lift off the obstruction and use the now-visible peg to correct the ring forward and slightly right. Bring the other ring to a left-side staging position, keeping it clear of the board.
Refine the ring's planar alignment from the head view and lower in short increments. Set the other ring down near the workspace boundary for a later right-arm pickup, without crossing either arm.
The peg appears at the upper-right edge of the red hole. Apply a millimeter-scale correction and lower gently. Release the staged ring on the table and withdraw the left arm.
Unload the ring slightly, make a final small fore-aft correction, and release to check settling. Move the left arm toward the single yellow piece while keeping the board clear.
The released red did not seat. Restore the right gripper to exact top-down and approach it afresh. Grasp and test-lift the yellow piece with the left arm.
Retry the corrected, previously unexecuted motion: stage the yellow near the workspace boundary and regrasp the flat red for a short test lift.
Yellow slipped, so clear the left arm to inspect its new location. Move the freshly grasped red over the third peg using the calibrated head-view offset, keeping its flat orientation.
Lower the red vertically with its hole now over the peg, retaining it for a seating check. Approach the fallen yellow and align the gripper with its sides instead of its corners.
The peg is now centered inside the red hole. Finish a short seating motion, release, and lift away. Regrasp the yellow across its sides and check it with a test lift.
The first red is visibly seated with the gripper open. Stage the securely held yellow nearer the boundary, and approach the second red without crossing arms.
The near-body staging location is too confined. Move the yellow back into clear left workspace before lowering the right gripper toward the second red; restore top-down alignment gently.
Move the yellow to a clear forward boundary staging spot while keeping it held. Finish the second red grasp and lift vertically clear of the table.
Replan from the interruption with smaller left increments and a lower approach height. Stage the yellow forward of the pieces; lift and carry the second red above its occupied peg.
Avoid further forward extension: set the yellow down at the current reachable boundary position. Align the second red above the seated first ring and lower cautiously.
Finish the second red's short seating descent, release, and inspect the stack. Withdraw the left arm diagonally backward from the staged yellow to maintain extension margin.
Both red rings appear seated and released. Approach the fallen blue with the left arm and the staged yellow with the right, keeping separate approach lanes and a low forward reach.
The tracking interruption shows the wrists crowded each other. Replan from observed poses and separate outward in small increments before resuming one-arm-at-a-time work near the center.
The previous attempt executed nothing. Use a backward left retreat that bridges the continuity guard, then separate both wrists outward before further manipulation.
Approach the staged yellow alone, lowering as the right arm reaches forward to preserve extension margin. Keep the left arm stationary and clear.
Use the wrist image to center the yellow before closing, then test-lift backward to reduce reach. Approach the fallen blue with the left arm on a separate rear lane.
Yellow is retained; retract from the forward reach while lifting and carry it above the fourth peg. Center the fallen blue, close, and test its retention with a short lift.
Align the held blue above its peg while correcting its yaw. Lower the yellow toward the short fourth peg with a small backward correction, retaining both pieces for inspection.
Lower both pieces slowly while retaining them. The short peg is visible near the yellow hole; check threading before release, and inspect the blue midway through insertion.
Tracking and RGB suggest contact between the nearby arms. Unload the blue and hold it high; release the visibly threaded yellow, then withdraw the right arm outward before resuming left insertion.
With the arms separated, restore the left wrist to level and lower the blue onto its peg with a small planar correction. Approach the remaining right-side blue bar independently.
Release the blue after the peg becomes visible through its hole and withdraw left to inspect settling. Fine-center the remaining right blue, close, and make a retention test lift.
The released blue is still tilted, so its group is unconfirmed. Carry the securely held right blue to a rear boundary staging area, while the left approaches the accessible star on its own side.
Center and grasp the left star, then test-lift. Set the held blue down gently at the rear boundary so it can later be handled by the left arm.
The star is retained. Lift it clear of the tall first peg and align above that peg, accounting for the grasp offset. Withdraw the open right arm from the staged blue into its own workspace.
Lower the first star with a small alignment correction and inspect threading while still holding. Independently approach the far-right star, restoring a level wrist with small increments.
The peg is visible within the star hole; release without further forcing and lift to inspect settling. Refine the far-right star approach and yaw while keeping its gripper open.
The first star missed and is now flat ahead of the board. Approach it for a fresh centered grasp. Close on the aligned far-right star, lift, and retract it within the right workspace.
Regrasp the flat left star with a small backward correction and lift fully above the tall peg. Hold the other star stationary in the right workspace to avoid inter-arm contact during insertion.
Use the fresh grasp's observed offset to align the left star with the tall peg, then begin a slow vertical insertion. Keep the right star held clear.
Apply a millimeter-scale correction toward the visible peg center and continue lowering slowly while holding, stopping short of release until threading is clear.
The star is tilting against the peg instead of sliding down. Lift clear to unload it, make a small backward correction, and inspect the hole-to-peg relationship before another descent.

The clear view shows the star hole substantially behind the peg because of its off-center grasp. Shift it forward while high, then make a short descent to check alignment rather than forcing insertion.
The peg moved toward the star hole as expected. Continue the measured forward correction with a very shallow descent, keeping both grasps closed and checking for true threading.
The peg now appears within the star hole. Keep the corrected planar alignment and descend vertically in small increments, retaining both pieces until seating is visible.
